title: Healthcare Data Warehousing, Interoperability and Clinical Data Standards
description: Twelve progressive challenges connecting hospital source systems, HL7, FHIR, terminology, warehouse modelling, governance and integration.

challenges.title: Healthcare data warehouse architecture
challenges.scenario: Distinguish operational systems, integration layers, staging, standardised clinical stores, dimensional marts and semantic/reporting layers.
challenges.tasks: Draw a source-to-report architecture for an outpatient medication utilisation dashboard. Identify data owners, refresh cadence, lineage, access boundaries and failure handling.
challenges.method: Use architecture.md and the Mermaid diagram. Identify OLTP vs OLAP workloads, fact grain, conformed dimensions, slowly changing dimensions and data lineage.
challenges.acceptance: Architecture identifies source, ingestion, staging, standardisation, warehouse/mart, BI and governance controls; each layer has a clear responsibility.
challenges.safety: Do not assume a warehouse is a direct copy of the EHR. Retain provenance and source meaning.

challenges.title: HL7 v2 message fundamentals
challenges.scenario: Read HL7 v2 segments, fields, components, delimiters, message types and control identifiers.
challenges.tasks: Parse a synthetic ADT^A01 admission message and identify MSH, EVN, PID, PV1 and message control ID. Explain acknowledgement and interface error handling.
challenges.method: Use the supplied HL7 v2 fixture and annotated walkthrough. Identify delimiters and segment boundaries.
challenges.acceptance: Correctly identify message type, sending/receiving application, patient identifier, visit identifier and admission event.
challenges.safety: HL7 v2 is event/message oriented; local implementation guides and profiles govern actual field use.

challenges.title: FHIR resources and REST basics
challenges.scenario: Understand FHIR resources, resource identity, references, bundles, profiles, extensions and REST interactions.
challenges.tasks: Inspect Patient, Encounter, MedicationRequest and Observation JSON examples. Trace references and explain why resource IDs differ from business identifiers.
challenges.method: Use FHIR R4 JSON fixtures and resource-reference map. Validate required fields conceptually and inspect Bundle entries.
challenges.acceptance: Resource types and references are correctly interpreted; no assumption that a resource is a flat table row.
challenges.safety: FHIR version and implementation guide must be known. The training examples are simplified and not a conformance claim.

challenges.title: FHIR search, bundles and pagination
challenges.scenario: Read FHIR search parameters, Bundle.total, next links, paging and server-side filtering.
challenges.tasks: Design a paginated extraction plan for encounters and observations. Preserve full next URLs, rate limits, retries and provenance.
challenges.method: Use API extraction design worksheet and mock Bundle fixtures. Contrast searchset and transaction bundles.
challenges.acceptance: Extraction plan handles pagination, duplicate resources, continuation tokens, failures and safe re-runs.
challenges.safety: Never assume one Bundle contains all matches. Follow server-provided paging links unchanged.

challenges.title: Clinical terminology systems
challenges.scenario: Differentiate ICD-10, SNOMED CT, LOINC, RxNorm and ATC and identify their appropriate use cases.
challenges.tasks: Map diagnosis concepts, laboratory observations, medication concepts and drug classes to the correct terminology family. Explain code, display, system URI and version.
challenges.method: Use terminology-reference.md and the local sample mapping table. Inspect code system URI and concept status.
challenges.acceptance: Each code is associated with the correct system and purpose; local labels are not presented as standard codes.
challenges.safety: Terminology licensing, jurisdictional editions, release versions and value sets matter. Do not invent mappings.

challenges.title: Terminology mapping and value sets
challenges.scenario: Create a governed crosswalk with source concept, target concept, mapping relationship, confidence, reviewer and version.
challenges.tasks: Review supplied sample crosswalk entries. Flag unverified local drug labels and ambiguous laboratory labels; separate exact, broader, narrower and unmapped cases.
challenges.acceptance: All mappings carry provenance, version, status and review trail; unmapped records remain visible rather than silently forced.
challenges.safety: The supplied ATC/LOINC examples are teaching fixtures and require verification against authoritative terminology releases before clinical use.

challenges.title: Clinical data integration and reconciliation
challenges.scenario: Integrate patients, encounters, medication requests and observations while preserving keys, timestamps, status and source lineage.
challenges.tasks: Build a curated dataset from synthetic CSV source tables. Check referential integrity, duplicate identifiers, date chronology and terminology coverage.
challenges.method: Run scripts/standardise_clinical_data.py and inspect the generated curated CSVs and quality report.
challenges.acceptance: Expected source counts reconcile: 80 patients, 120 encounters, 180 orders and 220 observations; all reference checks are documented.
challenges.safety: Do not merge patients on name or date of birth alone. This synthetic lab uses source IDs only.

challenges.title: FHIR-to-warehouse mapping
challenges.scenario: Translate FHIR resources into staging and dimensional tables with defined grain and reference handling.
challenges.tasks: Design fact tables for encounters, medication requests and observations; create patient, date, department and terminology dimensions.
challenges.method: Use sql/warehouse_schema.sql and fhir-to-warehouse-map.md. Load the curated outputs into SQLite for the exercise.
challenges.acceptance: Each fact table has a declared grain and stable source key; dimensions are conformed and duplicate facts are prevented.
challenges.safety: FHIR resource cardinality and lifecycle updates may require upsert/version handling, not simple append-only loads.

challenges.title: Interoperability security and governance
challenges.scenario: Apply least privilege, minimum necessary access, audit logging, transport security and data minimisation.
challenges.tasks: Write a data access and integration risk checklist for a remote analytics workflow. Identify PHI exposure points, secrets, logs and export controls.
challenges.method: Use governance-checklist.md and compare a safe vs unsafe integration design.
challenges.acceptance: Checklist covers authentication, authorisation, encryption, audit, retention, consent/legal basis as applicable, and incident response.
challenges.safety: Legal obligations depend on jurisdiction and organisation. Training notes are not legal advice.

challenges.title: Data quality and semantic validation
challenges.scenario: Validate units, value sets, status, dates, references, duplicate resources, terminology system URIs and missingness.
challenges.tasks: Run quality checks and classify issues as structural, referential, temporal, semantic or workflow-related. Prioritise by impact and likelihood.
challenges.method: Use supplied intentionally imperfect fixture rows and quality script outputs.
challenges.acceptance: Report quantifies each issue type, retains rejected/quarantined rows and documents corrective action.
challenges.safety: A value can be syntactically valid but clinically implausible; automated checks do not replace domain review.

challenges.title: End-to-end hospital interoperability project
challenges.scenario: Build a small reproducible source-to-warehouse pipeline from synthetic source files and FHIR-like resources.
challenges.tasks: Ingest, standardise, map, validate, load curated tables, produce audit outputs and document the lineage from source row to analytics fact.
challenges.method: Follow project-brief.md and run scripts/standardise_clinical_data.py; load schema into SQLite.
challenges.acceptance: All source counts, curated counts, quality findings and rejected records reconcile; project has README, data dictionary and limitations.
challenges.safety: This is a local educational pipeline, not a certified FHIR server or production interface engine.

challenges.title: Timed interoperability client simulation
challenges.scenario: Respond to a hospital request to integrate medication and laboratory information for an analytics dashboard.
challenges.tasks: In 120 minutes, deliver a source inventory, mapping decisions, data quality summary, curated extracts, warehouse schema and client handoff.
challenges.method: Use client-brief.md and rubric.json. Include assumptions, unresolved terminology, operational risks and acceptance evidence.
challenges.acceptance: Minimum 80/100 with no critical identity, terminology, grain or PHI-safety errors.
challenges.safety: Do not claim full FHIR or HL7 conformance based on these simplified fixtures.
